children: NVIDIA (NVDA) reportedly got orders for over 3 million RTX PRO 5500 cards from Chinese firms ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, reportedly valuing around $35 billion, about $11,400 per unit.
NVIDIA (NVDA) has pledged about $250 billion for supply-chain support and data-center buildout, potentially rising to $500 billion–$1 trillion if linked to added funding.
U.S. export controls and chip limits have halted NVIDIA (NVDA) sales in some Chinese markets; analysts say Chinese firms could gain if domestic supply chains improve.
NVIDIA (NVDA) sales depend partly on neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius; these smaller buyers have high debt and uncertain profits, risking lower demand and tighter margins if adoption slows.
Nancy Tengler says NVIDIA (NVDA) could double in 5–10 years even if earnings slow to 20–30%; previously saw near 96% growth and historically traded around a 13.5 earnings multiple.
NVIDIA joined TCV in a Series B extension for AI video startup Higgsfield. Higgsfield reported ~40M users and nearly $1B annualized revenue; growth ties to increased GPU and AI infra demand.
NVIDIA (NVDA) was cited for its agent-based AI and generative advances in video, text, code, robotics and drug research—capabilities linked to Kazakhstan’s national AI plans.
